prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet in this search. Across 7 earlier searches (84 trials), only one network family scored above 0, with a mean dev success of 0.22 in one world, and both of its seeds scored above 0. That family feeds the legal-action mask in as input channels under four layouts: as given, transposed, y-flipped and x-flipped. Its output maps are re-laid in the same four layouts and summed. Every other network and every recipe-only change scored exactly 0. This suggests worlds can differ from their descriptions in how actions are laid out, and the mask is the only reliable clue to that layout. The first priority is to reproduce this family at a training cost near the starting network's (r≈1), so the run keeps its full sample budget. The other two candidates each make one change to it: a recipe that gives more samples, and global context. A nonzero late training success is the first real signal.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials scored exactly 0 on both seeds, with late training success of 0 to 0.0003. Two of them were the four-layout family that worked in another world, one with more samples and one with global context. Uniform zeros mean something structural, not seed noise or sample count. The likely cause is that the action frame in this world differs from the observation frame in a way the four involution layouts (as given, transposed, y-flipped, x-flipped) do not cover. Candidates: a 90° or 180° rotation, a type-minor flat index (cell-major, type fastest), or DONE placed at index 0 so that every placement index shifts by one. Recipe changes are pointless until something learns. So this round tests three separate layout hedges on the same cheap trunk, one family of deviations each, so a nonzero result tells us which deviation applies. Training success above 0 is the first signal to look for.

### Round 3
All six trials scored 0 dev, with 0 late training success. The only hint of signal is 0.0003 for the plain four-layout baseline (r1c1). The tested hedges cover most action-frame deviations: 4 and 8 dihedral layouts, type-minor interleaving, a DONE-first shift, global broadcast and 2 PPO epochs. They all score 0, so a misaligned action frame of a simple kind is unlikely to be the main cause. Three causes are still untested: (1) learning is limited by too few gradient updates (the default gives only 32 updates); (2) the net cannot work out footprint landing and overhang relations precisely; (3) the observation groups are misaligned with one another (for example, the target in a different frame from the build), which no output re-layout can fix. Each candidate tests one of these on the r1c1 family. Any nonzero training success counts as the first real signal.

### Round 4
Every trial scored essentially zero. Only the four-layout net with small batches (r3c1, 128 updates instead of 32) scored above zero on dev: 0.002, from one seed at 0.0039. That is within seed noise. These all left training success at 0: eight dihedral layouts, type-minor index order, a DONE-first index shift, dihedral copies of the observation, a global broadcast and footprint pooling. Geometric and index hedges seem exhausted. The 1x1 stem can already learn any channel permutation, and the 3x3 trunk can learn anchor offsets. The one change that moved anything was the number of updates, a recipe change on the one family that learns. For this last round all three trials keep the r3c1 network and change only the recipe: (1) about 2x more updates again; (2) longer-horizon credit with gamma 0.99, in case this world's reward shaping differs and the exact-build bonus dominates; (3) fewer epochs, giving both more samples and more updates.

## Trial it ended with
name: Four-layout net, 4x more updates
hypothesis: Same network as r1c1 (the only trial with nonzero training success). The recipe changes to n_envs 64 and 16 minibatches, so the same 131k steps give 128 PPO updates instead of 32. With so few updates, PPO may stop long before the policy learns the precise fill decisions an exact build needs. If both seeds still show 0 training and 0 dev success, update count is not the bottleneck.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).

reply.evidence: Round 3 lists as an untested cause: "the observation groups are misaligned with one another (for example, the target in a different frame from the build), which no output re-layout can fix." That is the right kind of change: the target channels are offset from the build. But it never says the target is rolled 4 columns toward higher x with wraparound. Round 4 then drops the idea and moves on to recipe changes.
